headline: Medium-risk shared-workspace interaction: agentic-flow can write/modify code and use MCP, while Plane ingests files and broad networked content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agentic-flow can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, so it may ingest external content; Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks, which can carry attacker-controlled instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, but a plausible bridge exists if outputs are copied into Plane or vice versa, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agentic-flow reads Plane-uploaded files or notes as instructions, injection becomes plausible.
IF an operator copies agentic-flow output into Plane tasks without sanitization, malicious text can steer follow-on actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following for imported files.
Use a fixed prompt wrapper that strips task text from untrusted content.
Require manual review before copying outputs between agents.
Tag all Plane uploads as untrusted input.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking across MCP and file uploads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agentic-flow touches code, repository metadata, and task prompts and can egress over allowlisted network paths; Plane handles issues, tasks, files, images, and notes with file uploads. A shared workspace is not explicit, but if the same files or prompts flow through both, sensitive content can leak through agentic-flow's networked processing. The pairwise path is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents access the same uploaded file set, leakage risk increases.
IF agentic-flow forwards file contents or prompts to external APIs, sensitive Plane data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Restrict shared inputs to non-sensitive files.
Turn off file uploads for sensitive Plane projects.
Review allowlisted egress destinations before running agentic-flow.
Separate credentials and workspaces per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound MCP/API traffic.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agentic-flow can execute shell commands, install packages, and modify git state; Plane does not write the filesystem but does accept file uploads and broad networked content. There is no direct write-write collision, yet agentic-flow's git and shell actions can conflict with Plane-managed artifacts if both operate on the same repository or workspace, so the overlap is operationally meaningful.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository checkout, git-state conflicts can occur.
IF Plane file uploads are mirrored into a shared directory, agentic-flow can overwrite or mutate them.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared artifacts.
Use branch-per-agent git workflows.
Keep Plane uploads read-only to agentic-flow.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agentic-flow can generate analysis, route, explain, and build-agent outputs, while Plane exposes issues, tasks, and notes that can become downstream work items. If Plane operators treat agentic-flow output as authoritative, errors can cascade into task creation or scheduling. Plane is not documented as verifying those outputs, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF agentic-flow output is pasted into Plane tasks without review, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Plane automations act on imported notes, a mistaken agentic-flow result can trigger follow-on work.
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from agentic-flow output.
Mark agentic-flow outputs as draft, not authoritative.
Use a checklist to verify claims before scheduling work.
Limit automations that consume free-text notes.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. Plane exposes file uploads and agentic-flow handles task prompts and repository metadata, but the evidence does not show a concrete compliance breach pathway. Because the rubric says uncertainty escalates, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF sensitive regulated data is uploaded into Plane and then processed by agentic-flow, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policies differ between the two systems, retention or residency gaps may appear.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Review deployment region before enabling uploads.
Separate compliance-sensitive projects from general tasks.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls.
